subject: Secure SDLC artifacts request (CI/CD, secrets, code review)

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-corp.com>

Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com, security-reviewer@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Secure SDLC artifacts request (CI/CD, secrets, code review)

Hi Mina,

We're in the middle of our vendor intake for SOC 2 and the Acme security team has asked for artifacts demonstrating your Secure SDLC. Specifically we're collecting:
- CI/CD control descriptions and pipeline audit logs
- Code review policy and recent review evidence for a representative service
- Secrets management architecture and rotation policy
- Change management / deployment approval workflow evidence

Can you provide an index of evidence and concrete artifacts (logs, policy docs, screenshots) we can attach to our intake? We'd ideally have the first pass by next Wednesday so our auditor can review ahead of the planning meeting.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp
---
Attachment: acme_intake_form.pdf (pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC artifacts request (CI/CD, secrets, code review)

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is an index of the Secure SDLC evidence we've compiled and the first tranche of artifacts. Summary below and attachments included:

1) CI/CD controls
- Description: Our pipelines run in a locked-down GitOps model using GitHub Actions with enforced branch protections, signed commits, and required peer reviews.
- Evidence attached: cicd-pipeline-controls.csv (controls mapping), and a redacted pipeline audit log sample (linked in Drive).

2) Code review and approvals
- Policy: code-review-policy.md (attached) covers required reviewers, minimum approvals, and exemption process for emergency fixes.
- Evidence: sample PR export for service "inference-runtime" showing review history and reviewer IDs (redacted).

3) Secrets management
- Architecture: secrets-management-diagram.png (attached). We use a centralized KMS-backed secrets service with per-environment namespaces, automatic rotation for service credentials (30/90 day windows depending on secret type).
- Policy: rotation-policy.pdf (attached) and sample access lists.

4) Change management / deployment approvals
- We require JIRA ticket linked to pipeline and a separate approver group in GitHub. See INF-4789 for an example full lifecycle (link below).

I copied Rishi for the audit log snippets and any additional retention language. If you need formal signed attestations (e.g., a scanned statement for procurement), we can add that too — Laura can help with procurement coordination.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cSDLCArtifacts
JIRA: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-4789

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance (interim)
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: sdlc-evidence-index.pdf (pdf), cicd-pipeline-controls.csv (csv), code-review-policy.md (md), secrets-management-diagram.png (png), rotation-policy.pdf (pdf)

Tom / Mina —

Adding a few concrete items auditors typically ask for so you have them ready:
- Pipeline audit logs (redacted) covering the last 90 days for a representative repo — log contains run id, triggering user, commit hash, and runner id. We'll provide CSV export.
- KMS key rotation history (last 12 months) and who approved rotations. We can provide the rotation audit from our KMS and the HSM-backed key metadata.
- Recent vulnerability scan results for the repos used in the inference runtime (summary report).

Note on redaction: We'll truncate user emails to initials and remove any customer-specific data from logs.

Timeline — these artifacts will take a couple of days to coordinate across infra and platform teams. I can upload the pipeline logs and KMS rotation audit by Friday EOB PST. Mina / Laura: please confirm if procurement needs a notarized attestation or if a signed PDF from our security team is sufficient.

-Rishi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that looks great. For auditing purposes our checklist prefers:
- Pipeline logs (CSV) + short readme describing redaction
- KMS rotation audit (PDF export)
- Code review PR export (JSON or HTML) for one recent release
- A signed cover letter from your security team saying the artifacts are representative of normal operations

Procurement: procurement@acme-corp.com — we'll need the signed cover letter to attach to the vendor file. Is a signed PDF OK or do you require DocuSign?

If you can get the items by Friday EOB (your timezone) that keeps us on schedule. Appreciate the quick turn.

Tom
